Good Tuesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 517 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Carolyn DiPaolo for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: President Trump said today that he has called for a ban on U.S. diesel exports, joining other conservative voices who back the policy. Go deeper.
 
 
1 big thing — AI's next frontier: Cheaper power
 
Illustration: Lindsey Bailey/Axios

AI companies have competed on having the best and often most dangerous models for years. Now they're pivoting to a new focus: cost, Axios' Madison Mills reports.

🎉 Driving the news: It's modelpalooza in the AI world this week, with new releases from OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX and some Chinese providers.

  • Most of them are offering shocking levels of intelligence at prices that would've been unthinkable just a few months ago.
  • Top companies are finding a variety of ways to make powerful systems more efficient — for example, by using smaller portions of a model for some answers.

Zoom in: OpenAI is releasing GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna today, which bring down the cost for top business customers by 50% from previous iterations.

  • Anthropic is releasing Opus 5.5 today, which the company says costs around 40% less to run than Opus 5 while maintaining top intelligence.
  • Elon Musk's xAI yesterday released Grok 4.7, pitching the new model around price-performance. Yet in a testament to the sheer brutality of competition in the AI race, it only took 24 hours for new options to wipe out much of that price advantage.

Follow the money: A recent Citadel Securities report found that falling costs are fueling more use, and that overall AI spending is increasing.

  • That points to higher eventual profits for AI labs and related companies.

The bottom line: AI sticker shock feels like a distant memory, given the massive push to deliver cheaper models.

  • Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🏃‍♀️ Peloton makes a run for it
 
Peloton is introducing three new treadmills. Photo: Peloton

Peloton is debuting its first foldable treadmill and other models in a push to broaden its image beyond bikes and classes, Axios' Nathan Bomey reports.

👟 Its new treadmills, available Oct. 1:

  • Peloton Tread Flex (starting at $2,195): Its most affordable treadmill, with a foldable design.
  • Peloton Tread Vision ($3,495+): Features a "new cushioning system for greater comfort," plus a movement-tracking camera that "provides post-run form insights."
  • Peloton Tread+ Vision ($6,695+): The ultra-premium model offers an "incredibly soft, energy-returning slat belt" with AI-powered insights.

🤖 The company is also expanding its Peloton IQ software system to deliver new AI-powered insights to its runners based on their cadence, vertical oscillation and stride length.

Global labor markets are proving resilient even as corporate AI adoption accelerates.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
President Trump speaks to the United Nations General Assembly in New York today. Photo: Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images

4. 🍂 1 for the road: Happy equinox
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Astronomical fall begins at 8:05 p.m. ET tonight, when the Sun will shine directly over Earth's equator.

  • Afterward, for those of us in the Northern Hemisphere, days will get even shorter until December's winter solstice.
